text:
sre_ryan: FYI: BrightBasket is seeing repeated scale up/down churn on their Dedicated pool in eu-west-1 -> page from SE. They're getting 429s and a few high p95s, looks like autoscale flapping.

katie_custsuccess: Customer reports spikes correlate with their nightly ETL batch, but they say we've been smoothing previously. They opened a support ticket (BB-487).

alice_support: summary from ticket: 2026-03-17 01:12->01:40 UTC many 429s, request latency 800ms->3s, some auth failures intermittently. They attached request ids and a small sample.

sre_ryan: Attached Prom screenshots show replica count jumping 2->8->3 within 10m windows. CPU is low, but request queue length metric oscillates. Also seeing KV cache thrash metric incrementing. Paste of logs: 
```
[2026-03-17T01:15:03Z] tenant=brightbasket req_id=aa1bb status=429 reason=throttle_pool_downscale
[2026-03-17T01:16:27Z] tenant=brightbasket req_id=aa1cc status=200 latency=1250ms
[2026-03-17T01:18:01Z] tenant=brightbasket req_id=aa1dd status=403 auth=token_mismatch
```

oncall_bot: autoscaler: scale_up triggered for pool brightbasket-eu-west by metric: request_queue>250 for 30s
oncall_bot: autoscaler: scale_down triggered for pool brightbasket-eu-west by metric: idle_replicas>1 for 60s

eng_ana: Likely symptom of two interacting control loops: customer bursty traffic + our aggressive downscale cooldown. If queue spikes briefly we scale up, then quick idle detection scales down before cache/KV warms and latency climbs -> more queued requests -> repeat.

infra_miguel: Agree. Current config: scale_up_threshold=200, scale_up_window=30s, scale_down_threshold=50, scale_down_window=60s, cooldown=2m. For heavy KV-dependent workloads we should increase cooldown and use weighted queue metric that accounts for recent warmups.

alice_support: Customer also claims auth failures correlate with scale events. Could be token sync delay when new reps come up?

eng_ana: Possible. When we scale, instances fetch tenant keys from KMS/cache. If new replica hasn't populated local token cache, early requests may fail with 403 until sync completes. Need to check instance bootstrap logs.

sre_ryan: Repro steps requested by eng: can we simulate their nightly ETL load? They shared a lightweight script that sends bursts of concurrent requests with a warmup gap. They gave curl example: 
```
for i in {1..500}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"ping"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
sleep 15
# repeat 4x
```

katie_custsuccess: They've given time window when it happens (01:10-01:40 UTC), and said it used to be fine prior to last config change. Might be change deployed two days ago (autoscaler tuning).

infra_miguel: I can pull bootstrap logs for a replica bringup: command: `kubectl logs -l pool=brightbasket-eu-west -c agent --since=30m` — will look for key-sync and warmup events.

billing_bot: notice: BrightBasket has a burst billing cap configured; when they hit throttle we may be reinforcing throttles at the proxy layer. Check rate-limit headers from their sample.

alice_support: Sample header from failing request: `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `X-Proxy-Throttle: true`. So there is both pool-level throttle and proxy-level rate-limiter kicking in.

eng_ana: That doubles down on oscillation: pool scales down -> proxy enforces tenant token limit -> client retries -> short burst -> scale up -> new reps haven't warmed KV -> auth failures + queueing -> repeated. Two mitigation vectors: lengthen downscale cooldown and add grace period after scale up to treat replicas as warming (exclude from downscale and from auth gating until warmed).

sre_ryan: Proposed immediate mitigation (hotfix): increase scale_down_window to 5m and set scale_down_cooldown to 8m for that pool; set scale_up_grace=90s to avoid considering new replicas as fully ready for downscale and to delay proxy throttle enforcement for their tokens. Would like quick rollback plan.

infra_miguel: I can patch the pool config with `rctl apply --pool brightbasket-eu-west --set scale_down_window=300 --set cooldown=480 --set warmup_grace=90` and monitor. Will run in staging then prod.

katie_custsuccess: Customer ok with us doing config change during their quiet hour (they gave consent).

alice_support: Also opened ticket with SRE playbook: check KMS latency, instance bootstrap time, proxy throttle logs, and request id traces.

eng_ana: Long-term: add hysteresis to autoscaler using moving-average of queue over 3m and prefer gradual replica removal (drain connections instead of instant kill). Also add a KV prewarm hook on scale_up (kick warmup requests to new replicas).

sre_ryan: For now let's implement quick config bump and run the customer's repro script after change. Who can own running repro and validating?

infra_miguel: I'll deploy patch to staging now, run repro script against staging, collect metrics (replica count, queue, p95, auth error rate).

alice_support: I'll coordinate with BrightBasket to run their script against staging first and then prod when we confirm.

sre_ryan: Action items: Miguel -> patch + staging repro (ETA 45m). Ana -> add PromQL queries to monitor; sample query: `sum(rate(requests_queue[1m])) by (pool)` and `sum(increase(auth_failures[5m])) by (tenant)`. Alice -> keep customer updated. Katie -> file postmortem template after incident.

oncall_bot: incident: #BB-487 assigned to SRE oncall. Priority: P2.

alice_support: Noting also to check billing cap interactions; if proxy cancels requests due to cap, we may need to adjust messaging so customer's retries are backoff-friendly.

sre_ryan: Thanks team. We'll reconvene after staging run. If prod patch approved we'll schedule a 15m maintenance window and monitor 1:1 with BrightBasket. :thumbsup:

katie_custsuccess: Thanks all — keeping customer in loop.

eng_ana: quick note: add `--warmup-requests=10` to warmup hook so new replicas fetch KV early.

infra_miguel: staging run complete: initial results look promising, replica oscillation reduced, p95 improved from 1.8s peak to 350ms. Will prepare prod rollout plan.

sre_ryan: Marking this thread for postmortem follow-up.
